archetype.name: Improviser (scramble-first backup)
archetype.definition: An undrafted rookie fill-in whose legs move the offense better than his arm, keeping the passing game short and producing his best plays when the pocket breaks down.

report.headline: His legs worked, his arm didn't, and Mayfield's thumb decides what's next
report.take:
Jalon Daniels was Tampa Bay's emergency answer: an undrafted rookie from Kansas who replaced Baker Mayfield in Week 3 and started Weeks 4 through 6 while Mayfield's dislocated thumb healed. He went 1-2. The defense, fourth in EPA, kept those games close enough that a functional passer would have had a chance. As of October 20 he is listed as QB2 again, and Mayfield is 'supposed to practice' this week, so this card is about a player who may be going back to the bench.

The profile splits in two. As a runner he has been genuinely useful. He has 16 scrambles, they average +0.451 EPA each with seven first downs, and his 126 rushing yards rank ninth among 45 qualifiers despite only three starts. As a passer he has been among the league's worst. His 3.77 adjusted net yards per dropback ranks 43rd and his 5.1% interception rate also ranks 43rd. The approach is extremely conservative: an intended air yardage of 5.23 and an average throw landing 4.15 yards short of the sticks. That leaves the offense needing yards after the catch on almost every snap, and the passing offense sits 31st in EPA.

The passing problem is concentrated in two places. The first is the intermediate middle of the field. On 19 throws of 10-19 air yards he completed 26.3%, with a CPOE of -29 and two interceptions, which says he isn't reading or driving those windows yet. The second is the moment. In close fourth quarters he has posted -0.612 EPA per play with three interceptions on 22 attempts. The +1.036 EPA on nine deep balls and the three red-zone touchdowns look nice, but they rest on tiny samples. The 29 targets to Emeka Egbuka at -0.526 EPA apiece show the timing never clicked with the team's most-targeted receiver.

The game log isn't a learning curve. It mostly tracks the opponent. He was efficient against Dallas's 31st-ranked defense, posting +5.9 EPA, then collapsed against Pittsburgh's sixth-ranked unit: 22 of 43, five sacks, -21.8 EPA. He is a capable scrambler and a backup-grade passer. The best case for Tampa is that Mayfield's return makes the question moot.

strengths.title: Scrambles that actually pay
strengths.body: When the play breaks down, he leaves the pocket and gains real yardage. Scrambles make up 13% of his dropbacks and add clearly positive EPA, including seven first downs. Rushing is the one part of his game that has been above average in every start. It is a durable trait for a mobile quarterback, not a fluke.

strengths.title: Accurate when the ball is catchable
strengths.body: His bad-throw rate ranks third-lowest of 37 charted passers, and he completed 88% of throws behind the line. The misses aren't wild ones. The issue is where he chooses to throw and how the routes are timed, not raw ball placement. That gives a coaching staff something to build on, even if it won't fix the intermediate problem quickly.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing, small sample
strengths.body: All three of his touchdown passes came on nine red-zone throws, worth +0.412 EPA per play. In a compressed field his short, quick style fits better. Nine plays is a hint rather than a trait, and it won't hold at this rate.

concerns.title: No answer between 10 and 19 yards
concerns.body: The intermediate zone is where NFL passing games live, and he has been close to unplayable there. He completed about a quarter of those throws, with two interceptions and a CPOE of -29. That pushes the offense into checkdowns, which is why his average throw lands well short of the sticks. For an undrafted rookie this is the classic gap in processing and anticipation, and it rarely closes within a single season.

concerns.title: Turnovers in close games
concerns.body: Every one of his five interceptions came with the game within one score, and three came in close fourth quarters, where he has posted -0.612 EPA per play. He has protected the ball well as a runner, with no fumbles lost. The problem is late-game throws into coverage while trying to make something happen, and it turned two winnable games into losses.

concerns.title: Good defenses overwhelm him
concerns.body: Against Pittsburgh's sixth-ranked defense he took five sacks and posted -21.8 EPA, by far his worst start. He was efficient only against Dallas's 31st-ranked unit. His rapport with Egbuka never formed, at -0.526 EPA per target on 29 targets, which removes the offense's top option.

trend.note: His three starts tracked the opponent: a modest negative game against Green Bay, a clean win against Dallas's 31st-ranked defense, then a 43-attempt, five-sack collapse against Pittsburgh. There's no steady improvement underneath the swings.

nextGame.headline: Likely back on the bench; a soft pass rush if not
nextGame.body:
If Daniels starts at Carolina, the matchup suits his style better than Pittsburgh did. The Panthers rank 27th in quarterback hit rate and 21st in sack rate, so he should face less of the pressure that buried him in Week 6. Their defense is middling overall, 19th in EPA and 16th against the pass. The catch is that they limit explosive passes, allowing the third-lowest rate in the league, so he would have to string together short completions and scrambles, which is exactly where he's been weakest. Carolina's offense ranks eighth in passing EPA and leans pass-heavy. If Tampa falls behind, the game could force him into the late, close-game throwing that has produced most of his interceptions. The Book has Tampa as a 3.5-point road underdog.

Availability is the real story. Mayfield (dislocated thumb) is listed Out with a projected return on game day, and the head coach says he is 'supposed to practice' Wednesday. Daniels is already back at QB2 on the depth chart. A full practice week for Mayfield most likely means Daniels is the backup again. On Carolina's side, defensive tackle Cam Jackson is on injured reserve, which thins an already modest interior pass rush. Starting tackle Monroe Freeling missed last week with a knee injury, which could help Tampa's defense get stops and keep the game script calm.

keyMatchups.title: Light pass rush versus his escapes
keyMatchups.body: Carolina rarely gets home on the quarterback, and Jackson's absence removes another interior body. More clean pockets should mean fewer of the sacks that wrecked his Pittsburgh start. His best plays come when he extends and runs, though, and a calmer pocket offers fewer of those chances.

keyMatchups.title: Explosive passes shut down
keyMatchups.body: Carolina allows one of the league's lowest explosive-pass rates, which takes away the few deep shots that boosted his numbers. That leaves him needing sustained drives through the intermediate area, his worst zone.

keyMatchups.title: Mayfield's practice status
keyMatchups.body: The thumb report decides whether any of this matters. If Mayfield practices fully, Daniels is a clipboard holder in Week 7.

nextGame.watch: Whether Mayfield practices fully on Wednesday. Then, if Daniels starts, whether he can complete anything between 10 and 19 yards.

restOfSeason.body:
The most likely path is that Mayfield reclaims the job within a week, and Daniels returns to the backup role with occasional relief snaps. If he does start again, expect more of the same. His rushing value is real and repeatable, roughly 25-45 yards a start on scrambles, but the passing will stay short, low-yield and turnover-prone until the intermediate reads improve, which three NFL starts give no sign of yet.

Some numbers should move. His red-zone touchdown rate and deep-ball efficiency rest on nine attempts each and will cool. His interception rate is likely to come down somewhat from the bottom of the league, and his sack rate should ease against weaker pass rushes. Neither change turns him into an average starter. The projections below are per start, not per game, because as a backup most of his games would produce close to nothing.
swingFactors: Mayfield's thumb recovery and any setback
Strength of opposing pass rushes if he starts
Whether he connects with Egbuka over the middle

confidence.note: Three starts, a backup role again, and a starting job that depends on Mayfield's injury timeline.
